title: A Sandstorm in a Room
subtitle: A tiny grain of sand slips into the eye, causing tears to well up in response.

items.text: A Sandstorm in a Room
The piston rotates on the floor like a toy top.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hmm. I am not in a suitable form to receive a guest.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Simone, can you put me back in my body?
Her assistant rushes over and puts her into a robot body.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I feel much better. Thank you.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh, you have even put on a face for me. How sweet of you.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I have noticed your icy gaze, Researcher Adler. You are yearning to correct the logic of this place.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Well, I only said that to Simone out of courtesy. In reality, whichever body I am put into makes no difference to me.
Her ill-timed explanation annoys him even more.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The experiment, ma'am. Why hasn't it stopped?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Are you going to pretend that nothing's happened? That no one died?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Could it be that you and Ulrich, "the Awakened," being the tin cans you are, have no regard for actual lives?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Adler Hofmann, I will not warn you again ...
Ulrich storms back into the room with two guards, ready to throw him out at any moment.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Relax, Adler. You are led by a biased opinion because you lack critical information. A common defect in all cognitive processes.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I believe you will shift to a more rational perspective once you receive sufficient information on the subject.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: "A more rational perspective"?!
The human, known for his logical thinking, responds with an overwhelming amount of feeling.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We are humans, not machines! We are not expendable parts!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I have plenty of reasons to question your decisions. Your excessive insistence on this experiment could be a sign of uncontrollable behavior, a trait commonly seen in arcanists.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The experiment has been canceled everywhere.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Except for this very room.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What?
The robot flashes a smile, as if anticipating the man to be pleased with her response.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: As you and Researcher Medicine Pocket have said, the ritual is beyond the limits of almost everyone here. The side effects will kill them before the ritual can even take effect.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The first wave was inevitable. Dora had pressed send before she disintegrated. We only managed to halt the subsequent transmissions, and evacuate the unaffiliated staff.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We kept only a few arcanists on the team, and each has signed the consent form.
Mutual consent. That bloody form again.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Forgive me, ma'am, but I have to use your argument against you.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You, too, are guided by a biased opinion—an overly optimistic one—because you have failed to properly assess the risks involved. We have suffered enough misfortunes just by uttering a few syllables of the incantation!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: We've talked about the "limit" of things before. You should know better and ask the rest of the team to quit the experiment. Your insistence will only bring calamity upon calamity on our people, for nothing!
The researcher fights to stay calm, reiterating his views he had already shouted in the hallway.
Ulrich begins his retort, but the director simply nods in agreement.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. You might be right.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But how is "being right" going to help us?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Huh?
She grins, trying for a warm, gentle smile, but it comes across as anything but.
Enigma despised that face. Every time she tried to show a hint of humanity, it only served to highlight how different she was from everyone else.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You spoke of the "limit."

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And I am surprised that it is you who brought it up.
Enigma pauses for a second, not sure if she's being sarcastic.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The physical appearance of humans has remained relatively unchanged since the Neolithic era, but their thoughts and civilization continued to evolve and underwent significant transformations.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The achievements that humanity enjoys today were not given to the species by any one person with godlike powers, but were the result of the collective efforts of all human beings.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Limits and boundaries must be pushed, or there would never have been room for development. There is no reason to believe that the limit cannot be challenged, especially when we already have the tools to do so.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We must make progress happen.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Grandiose lies.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Lies?
Oh, crap. He forgot about her excellent hearing.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We have no choice but to go beyond that limit.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If we do not break away from the "Storm," there is no future for us, let alone progress.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We need to first determine all the side effects as a priority. This important step will help us compile data and eliminate the effects, so our colleagues can use the ritual safely.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And who will try it this time, Madam Lucy? You're not going to test the side effects at the cost of lives, are you?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: No. Thanks to Ulrich, we stumbled upon a breakthrough.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You are right. It is time to send the other arcanists home. Only the Awakened are needed here.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: The Awakened?
The tungsten wires glow faintly red in the dark, then the room is lit.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: The power is back, ma'am. We are ready to resume.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. It will take time to properly explain.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Please wait, Adler. We have yet to reach an agreement.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What? Are you experimenting? Here?
Ignoring his surprise, Lucy sits down on the iron bench.
Wires of various sizes are attached to her body.
The instrument comes to life to the piston's rhythm, faithfully recording every change in the robot.
From her slightest movements to arcane fluctuations, nothing goes unnoticed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: La unua ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Wait. She's reciting it?
Frozen in place by the scene, he looks around the room in disbelief.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: She's read the reports, right? She was there when Dora broke into pieces!
Rarely does her back curl up like this.
The usual cheerful expression on her face has changed to one of unease, suggesting that something is amiss.
A hunk of metal should not feel pain. They have no flesh, no nerves.
But if she is in agony, what could be the cause of such torment?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: ... Urrm ...
Will she break apart, too? Like those people?
The ominous "curse" has set its sights on its prey.
It watches, almost like Zeus on a mountaintop, ready to unleash lightning on the mortals who dare to steal fire.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: No, Simone ... I ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I cannot ... continue ...

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Urgh ... Urrh ...
The most primal, instinctual fear.
This is the first time he's ever heard her emotions pour out so raw.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: You fools, don't just stand there! Stop her! Now!
Panic and horror twist in his stomach. He has an irresistible urge to rip out the wires and put an end to her torture.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Who's going to lead us if she also turns into a pile of scraps?!

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Stay where you are, Enigma!
Ulrich's voice, full of animosity, comes from behind.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: You insisted on being here. You demanded to see this.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Don't bring your pathetic, narrow-minded humanitarian values in here and tell us what to do. What do you know about us?
Simone leans over to her. She speaks softly.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: You can do it, madam. This is just part of the established procedures.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Just a few more syllables, madam, and it will be over.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Established ... procedures ...
Fear ebbs away a little as she repeats those words.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I like ... that ...
Her eyes close. She forces out the last word with great determination.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Cir ... klo.
It is done.
A clear, accurate, impeccable read.
Right at that moment, the lights in the lab go out.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: *sigh* Was that all, Simone?

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: Yes.
No one can see her face in the darkness.
But Enigma believes it to be a smile.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Good.
A gust of sand rises in the room.
Without warning and out of nowhere, it screams through the enclosed darkness.
The raging storm engulfs the robot's cold metal body, carrying her away with great force.
When the sand subsides, all that remains is an old piston, clattering to the ground.
"Clang."
TO BE CONTINUED…
